owning_issue.body:
## Purpose and current authority

Prepare the first bounded scientific work order for full original-function HydrAMP modernization: **deterministic encoder/posterior-parameter inference**, enabling a later analogue increment. Parent planning: #4. Consumer: https://github.com/uibcdf/peptidemt/issues/32.

The investigator has requested preparing this increment. The contract below is **proposed for review**, not approval to implement all original functions, load learned weights, run a new model campaign, train or contact authors. Accepted dev3/D41 remains frozen.

## Source-level findings

Original source `6590d2f4c2963f25d30669052a4c4a857e0e7279`, selected starter `7804df862872ccc6d09fe01c41bafbca194cfa31`.
- Selected encoder: vocabulary 21, 25 positions, embedding 100; two concatenating bidirectional 128-unit reset-before GRUs; first returns a sequence, second final states; two 256→64 linear heads.
- The actual saved GRU metadata specifies tanh/sigmoid, reset_after=False and implementation 2. Do not infer those from framework defaults or substitute native torch.nn.GRU.
- Original `z_sigma` is used through `exp(z_sigma/2)` to obtain standard deviation. Preserve it as the native log-variance parameter, not an already evaluated standard deviation.
- Existing 42-entry header inventory supplies all 17 encoder weight headers. Six saved JSON configurations are available. No parameter array is opened/deserialized in preparing this issue.

## Proposed contract

Input: nonempty CPU int64 tensor [N,25], values 0..20. Preserve all rows/order/duplicates and zero positions; mask_zero=False includes the learned zero embedding. No strings, FASTA, truncation, repair, sorting or molecular realization in this operation.

Outputs: deterministic CPU float32 mean [N,64] and native log-variance parameter [N,64], preserving original latent coordinates and occurrence order. Public names/classes are illustrative until agreed. No posterior sample, standard-deviation/noise computation, RNG mutation, PCA, decoder/head/descriptor/analogue call or training.

Reuse the owner’s existing reset-before cell and weight validation where scientifically valid; add bidirectional sequence handling with verified direction/concat/time alignment. Preserve accepted inference-core behavior and artifact identities. A future implementation gets a separate local candidate; do not overwrite dev3.

## Gates to prepare

1. Review scientific input/output meanings, failure behavior and scope before implementation.
2. After approval, synthetic-weight tests against an independent reference: reset-before/gate order, backward time alignment, forward/backward concatenation, unmasked zeros, both heads, row/duplicate correspondence, invalid input/metadata rejection and no RNG mutation.
3. Qualify the separate installed candidate with original decoder/head regressions as applicable; do not mistake synthetic tests for pretrained proof.
4. Before any real parameters/model execution, present a separate exact artifact/input/runtime/host/call plan. The reference should target the original encoder parameters without constructing the full generator/PCA; report actual loader/graph behavior and all calls. Old model budgets are exhausted.
5. Preserve unchanged diagnostic bands as existing reports only; encoder scientific acceptance and any prospective numerical criterion require an explicit reason/review before real output is observed.

Local consumer work order will be `devguide/hydramp_encoder_work_order.md`; owning snapshot `devguide/pytorch_encoder_work_order.md` in the modern worktree. This issue remains open until the scoped preparation/implementation/qualification receives its actual disposition. Original optional-filter defects remain separately in #7 and do not block deterministic encoder preparation.

No models/frameworks imported, weights/PCA loaded, encoder/other neural/descriptor call, training, GPU, package publication, commit/push or author contact in preparation. This issue preserves an actionable proposal; it does not create a new accepted scientific decision.
